protocol.name: cupertino_host_v1

description.summary: private protocol between the Cupertino server, a shell host and its components

protocol.description:
A shell host is a process that runs components of the shell, each on a thread and a connection of its own. The server starts the host on a connection that holds the host role and nothing else, tells it which components it runs, and hands it one connection per component on request; a component's roles are bound to that connection and end with it. The host reports what it observes of each component (busy, unresponsive, lost, failed), and the server decides what follows: when a component starts again, when it stops, and which host runs it. A component holds its roles in one host at a time.
The protocol is private: the server and the hosts are built from one source. Every change of a message raises the version of its interface, and a message added after version 1 carries the version that added it. A host binds an interface only at the version it was built with: a host that finds another version of cupertino_host_v1 exits with status 76 without binding it, and one that finds another version of an interface a component binds starts no component on that connection (cupertino_host_component_v1.unavailable).

interface.name: cupertino_host_v1

description.summary: a shell host

interface.description:
Global singleton, offered only to a connection the server made for a host process it started. The connection holds the host role alone: it sees this global and the core globals, and none of the roles of the components.
Right after binding the server sends kind, then the component list: one component event for each component this host runs, followed by done. Whenever the list changes the whole list is sent again, and each list replaces the one before. For a component of the list the host creates its object with get_component and asks for its connection. A component that left the list is stopped by the host, which then destroys its object.
A host is shared or separate. The shared host runs every component that no separate host runs, and is the hub of the host bus, the message bus of the components. A separate host runs one component and reaches the host bus through a socket pair the server makes: one end goes to the shared host (bus_peer), the other to the separate host (bus). A session has at most one shared host; while components run, it has exactly one, also when its list is empty.
The server ends a host it expects to exit (after restart, after cupertino_host_component_v1.lost from a separate host, after an empty list of a separate host) when the host has not exited within 2 seconds, by killing its process.

entry.name: component
entry.summary: the host already holds an object for that component

entry.name: kind
entry.summary: a request only one kind of host may make came from the other

entry.name: name
entry.summary: not a name of the server's component table

entry.name: shared
entry.summary: runs the components no separate host runs and is the hub of the host bus

entry.name: separate
entry.summary: runs one component and reaches the host bus through the shared host

request.name: destroy

description.summary: unbind the host global

request.description: Component objects created through this global stay valid.

event.name: kind

description.summary: what this host is

event.description: Sent once, before the first list.

event.name: component

description.summary: a component this host runs

event.description: The name is one of the server's component table (at most 32 bytes of lower-case ASCII letters). The components sent since the last done are the whole list. A name the host does not hold a component for is answered with get_component and unavailable.

event.name: done

description.summary: end of a component list

event.description: A list may be empty: the host then runs no component. A separate host whose list is empty stops its component and exits successfully; it does not wait for a thread that does not end.

request.name: get_component

description.summary: the host's object for one component

request.description:
Creates the object the host reports the component's state on and receives its connection on. Posts the name error for a name that is not in the server's component table, so a host holds at most one object for each component of the table, and the component error when the host already holds an object for the name.
A name of the table that is not in the host's current list is not an error, since the list may have just changed: the object is inert, and a connect on it waits. The object becomes live when a later list holds its name, and a waiting connect is answered then. The host destroys an inert object when the next list arrives without the name.

request.name: request_restart

description.summary: ask to be restarted at a quiet moment

request.description: The host holds a thread it cannot end (a component that was lost, a helper thread that does not stop) and asks to be started afresh. To a shared host the server answers with restart once the seat has had no input for two seconds and no component of this host holds a grab or shows a transient surface, and at the latest 60 seconds after the request. To a separate host it answers at once. A restart asked for this way is not counted as a crash of the host. Asking again before the answer changes nothing.

event.name: restart

description.summary: the quiet moment came

event.description: The answer to request_restart: the host stops its components and exits, without waiting for a thread that does not end. The server starts it again at once, with the list it has then. The persistent surfaces of its components are held meanwhile (cupertino_component_v1.persist).

event.name: component_stopped

description.summary: the server gave a component up

event.description: Sent to the shared host when the server stops starting a component by itself (cupertino_host_component_v1.stopped), whichever host ran it. The shared host says so on the host bus, where it alone publishes what the host says.

event.name: bus_peer

description.summary: the shared host's end of a bridge to a separate host

event.description:
Sent to the shared host for each separate host: fd is one end of a Unix stream socket pair the server made, and the separate host that runs component holds the other end. The descriptor is the peer: no path names the socket and no other process can connect to it. The shared host takes every message that arrives on it as that component's and closes it when a message names another sender.
Sent again, with the end of a fresh pair, when either host has started again and after bus_dropped for the component; the shared host closes the end it held. The descriptor is close-on-exec and must stay so.

event.name: bus_peer_gone

description.summary: a separate host ended

event.description: The separate host that ran component is gone, and the shared host closes its end of the bridge to it.

event.name: bus

description.summary: a separate host's end of the bridge to the shared host

event.description: Sent to a separate host: fd is the other end of the pair of bus_peer. Sent again, with the end of a fresh pair, when the shared host has started again and after bus_dropped; the separate host closes the end it held. Until the first arrives, and while no shared host runs, the component's messages to other components wait in the separate host. The descriptor is close-on-exec and must stay so.

request.name: bus_dropped

description.summary: an end of a bridge closed or failed

request.description: The bridge between the shared host and the separate host that runs component closed, or broke one of its rules. Either side may say so; a separate host names its own component. The server makes a fresh pair and sends its ends with bus_peer and bus, no sooner than one second after the pair before. Posts the name error for a name that is not in the component table and the kind error from a separate host that names another component than its own.

interface.name: cupertino_host_component_v1

description.summary: one component, as its host sees it

interface.description:
The host asks for the component's connection with connect and starts the component when connection arrives. While the component runs, the host watches whether its loop returns to its wait and reports busy, unresponsive, responsive and lost. When the component ends without being asked to, the host reports failed and asks for a connection again; the server decides when it comes.
The server keeps the component's failures: they outlive this object and the host. A failure is a failed request or a lost request. A component that failed starts again no sooner than 0.25 seconds after the failure, a time that doubles with each failure up to 8 seconds and starts over once the component ran for 60 seconds. Five failures within 60 seconds stop it (stopped) until the person asks for a restart or logs in again. A loss takes ten seconds or more to be declared, so the run of an instance that is lost within 60 seconds of its start is left out of those 60 seconds: a component that hangs at every start is stopped at its fifth loss.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: give the component up

request.description: Sent once the component has stopped, when a list leaves it out or the host exits. The server closes the component's connection if it is open.

request.name: connect

description.summary: ask for the component's connection

request.description: The host has no running instance of the component and is ready to start one. The server first closes any connection it holds for the component in this host, then answers with connection when the component may start, or with stopped. One answer is outstanding at most: asking again before it arrives changes nothing.

event.name: connection

description.summary: the component's connection

event.description: The client end of a connection that holds the component's roles and no other, valid while this host process lives. The host starts the component on it. The descriptor is close-on-exec and must stay so: no child of the host inherits it.

event.name: stopped

description.summary: the component stays stopped

event.description: Sent in place of connection: the server starts the component no more by itself. The persistent surfaces the server held for it are released. A connection event follows when the person asks for a restart of the component.

event.name: restart

description.summary: stop the component and start it again

event.description: The person asked for a restart of the component while it runs: the host stops it, as for a component that leaves the list, and sends connect. Not counted as a failure. The person's request is answered when the component sends cupertino_component_v1.ready, and with an error when it has not within 10 seconds of its connection.

request.name: busy

description.summary: the component's loop has not returned to its wait

request.description: The component's loop has been out of its wait for a whole interval of the host's watchdog: the watchdog, which checks every 0.5 seconds after a start-up grace of 10 seconds, found it out of its wait at two checks in a row with no return between them. A loop that one check catches in the middle of a turn is not busy. The server stops waiting for the component where it would: a transaction that expects it starts without it.

request.name: unresponsive

description.summary: the component has been busy for two seconds

request.description: The server releases the component's grabs, dismisses its transient surfaces, returns the keyboard focus to the window that had it and sends the component no input. Its persistent surfaces keep their place and their picture.

request.name: responsive

description.summary: the component's loop is back in its wait

request.description: Ends busy and unresponsive: the component gets input again, and what it shows from then is shown.

request.name: lost

description.summary: the component has been busy for ten seconds

request.description:
The host has shut the component's sockets down, taken it off the host bus and dropped the results of its tasks; its thread cannot be ended. The server counts a failure and holds the component's persistent surfaces. It takes the component out of this host's list and, when the failure's restart time has passed, starts it alone in a separate host, where it stays for the rest of the session or until the person asks for a restart of the component.
A shared host follows with cupertino_host_v1.request_restart. A separate host exits at once, without waiting for the thread; the server kills it when it has not exited within 2 seconds. That exit is not counted as a crash of the host.

entry.name: panic
entry.summary: the component, one of its tasks or one of its helper threads panicked

entry.name: error
entry.summary: its loop ended with an error: a protocol error or a connection that closed

entry.name: exit
entry.summary: its loop returned without being asked to stop

request.name: failed

description.summary: the component ended without being asked to

request.description: The host has torn the component down and shut its sockets. The server counts the failure, whatever its cause, and holds the component's persistent surfaces. Posts the cause error for a value that is not an entry of failure.

entry.name: absent
entry.summary: the host was built without the component

entry.name: version
entry.summary: the connection offers another version of an interface the component binds than the host was built with

request.name: unavailable

description.summary: this host does not run the component

request.description: The host starts no instance of the component. The server leaves it stopped in this host and logs it; it is not counted as a failure. When the host is one of the development folder, the server runs the component in the installed host instead. Posts the reason error for a value that is not an entry of unavailable_reason.

interface.name: cupertino_component_v1

description.summary: what a component tells the server about itself

interface.description:
Global singleton, offered only on a connection the server handed out through cupertino_host_component_v1.connection. Right after binding the server sends component, then one hold event for each surface it holds from the component's earlier instance, followed by done.
Programs the server starts as processes of their own (the lock screen, the prompts, the screenshot program) do not see this global: the server knows each by its process.

entry.name: invalid_surface
entry.summary: the surface belongs to another client, is gone or is not a layer shell surface

entry.name: mapped
entry.summary: the surface already committed a buffer

entry.name: key
entry.summary: a key that is empty, over 64 bytes, or already names another surface of the connection on the same output

request.name: destroy

description.summary: unbind the global

request.description: The accepted bus name and the persistent surfaces stay as they are.

event.name: component

description.summary: the component this connection belongs to

event.description: The name of the component whose roles the connection holds, and the number of this instance: the count of the connections the server has handed out for the component in this session, starting at 1. The instance number is part of the name of every transaction the instance creates (cupertino_transaction_manager_v1.create), so the transactions of a restarted component are never taken for those of the instance before.

event.name: hold

description.summary: a surface held from the earlier instance

event.description: The server keeps the last picture and the reserved space of a persistent surface of this component whose connection ended, with its holes and their claims. key is the key that surface was persisted with.

description.summary: end of the holds

request.name: announce_bus_name

description.summary: the component's connection to the session bus

request.description:
The unique name (":1.42") of the bus connection the component owns its well-known names on. The server answers with bus_nonce, and the component proves that the connection is its own by calling AnnounceComponent of org.cupertino.Session1 with the nonce from that bus connection. The answer to the whole is bus_name.
The server accepts when the call's sender is the announced name, the nonce is the one of this announcement, unused and at most 5 seconds old, the bus daemon gives the sender's process as the host process this connection was handed to, and the name is accepted for no other component. Being in the same process as another component proves nothing: a name already accepted for another component is refused, and that component keeps it.
Until the acceptance, and after a refusal, the server takes a bus call from the component as an unknown caller's. From the acceptance on it takes a call from that name as this component's, and a call from another connection of the same process as not this component's. Announcing again takes the accepted name away until the fresh announcement is accepted. Posts the name error for a string that is not a unique bus name.

event.name: bus_nonce

description.summary: what the component returns over the session bus

event.description: The answer to announce_bus_name: 32 lower-case hexadecimal digits the server drew at random for this announcement. The nonce is good for one call of AnnounceComponent, whatever its answer, within 5 seconds. It is sent on this connection and nowhere else.

entry.name: accepted
entry.summary: the component called with the nonce from the announced name

entry.name: refused
entry.summary: the call came from another name or process, the name is another component's, or no call came in time

event.name: bus_name

description.summary: whether the announced name is the component's

event.description: Sent once for each announcement: when the call with its nonce was judged, or 5 seconds after bus_nonce when none came. A refused name leaves the component without a bus identity: the server treats its bus calls as an unknown caller's.

request.name: persist

description.summary: make a layer shell surface persistent

request.description:
A surface is transient unless it is persisted. When the component's connection ends, or the component is reported unresponsive, the server dismisses its transient surfaces at once. A persistent surface is held instead when the connection ends: its last picture stays where it is with its reserved space, every animation of its layers at its end, and takes no input.
A held surface keeps its holes (cupertino_hole_v1): each goes on drawing its source, a window live, and a claim stays in force, so a claimed window stays in its hole and takes no input there. The placements a window manager committed (cupertino_window_manager_v1) are held as long as a hold of that component lasts on the output. No window comes back on screen or moves because a component restarts.
key names the surface among the component's persistent surfaces on its output and is the same for each instance of the component. When this connection persists a surface with the key of a hold on the same output, that surface takes the hold over: with its first commit that attaches a buffer, in the same frame, the held picture goes and the surface shows in its place, the held holes and claims give way to the holes and claims of that commit, and the held placements of the output give way to the placements this connection committed before it, which the server keeps until that frame. A connection that has committed no placement by then leaves the held ones in force until its first commit of placements. The reserved space passes to the surface without the usable area changing in between; when the surface asks for another exclusive zone than the held one, the usable area changes once, in that frame.
Sent before the surface's first commit that attaches a buffer. Posts invalid_surface for a surface that is not a layer shell surface of this client, mapped for one that already committed a buffer, and key for an empty key, one over 64 bytes or one that already names another surface of the connection on the same output.

request.name: ready

description.summary: the component has shown what it shows at start

request.description: Every hold of the earlier instance that no surface took over ends: its picture goes, its space is given back and its claims end, and the held placements of its output give way to the placements this connection committed, or end when it committed none. A window that a claim or a placement lets go moves to where it shows without it along the server's return motion. Without this request the server ends those holds 10 seconds after it handed the connection out. A restart the person asked for is answered when this request arrives.
